structured_output.summary: Architect review of the tie-capacity design (attempt 2, commit 8f9f28e) against STD-ARCH v2.0, STD-SAFETY v3.1 and STD-GOV v1.1. One VIOLATION, STD-ARCH-4: the new public function flisr.tie_capacity_verdict does not state its behaviour for out-of-range transferred_kw (L < 0, ±inf, NaN) or a naive as_of, and a negative or -inf L closes the tie (measured: Section accepts -120.0 / -inf / nan; -120 <= 0+0.5 is True). The design must state fail-safe behaviour, or raise a spec question if a new reason code is needed. Every other clause conforms: ARCH-1/2 (under the scoped Q-DESIGN-1 waiver), ARCH-3/5/6/7/8, SAFETY-1..6/8, GOV-1/2/6. Five non-blocking observations, including that the DEF-FLISR-7 fix branch adds a guard in the same tie loop. The design was not edited. The review was committed to agent/feature-tie-capacity/architect @ 0584fbb with the AI-Governance trailer; no PR was opened, following the earlier stages.

evidence.detail: VIOLATION A-1: design §3 docstring of public tie_capacity_verdict covers absent/invalid kw/lead/quality/stale only. No stated behaviour for transferred_kw outside L>=0 (spec §0) or for a naive as_of. The close condition L <= C+0.5 closes on L=-120 or -inf (not fail-safe). The §8 claim of full coverage is inaccurate.

evidence.detail: Section accepts load_kw -120.0, -inf (incl. JSON -Infinity), nan. Close condition: L=-120 True, L=-inf True, L=+inf False, L=nan False. naive as_of - aware timestamp raises TypeError.
Section.load_kw: float = 0.0, unconstrained, so out-of-range L is reachable from the network model.
Fail-safe preferred; out-of-range L is not refused (part of A-1). Otherwise the minimal positive-close design removes today's NaN/+inf close.
